newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: SAB awaits go-ahead on Namibian brewery.
newsitem.headline: SAB awaits go-ahead on Namibian brewery.

text.p: South African Breweries (SAB) said it was awaiting a response from the Namibian government on plans to build a brewery at Oshakati near the northern Angolan border.

"We have put in an application for a brewery at Oshakati a month ago and hope for a response from the Namibian government," Andre Parker, managing director of SAB's international beer business, told Reuters.
He said if SAB was granted permission to build the brewery, involving an investment of around one million rand ($217,000), it would be the company's first in Namibia.
Building would take about 18 months, Parker added.
Parker said the brewery would also serve the unexplored market in southern Angola, although the company is hoping to take over a brewery in the southern Angolan town of Lubango.
According to SAB's Namibian proposal, 51 percent of the shares would be owned by local entrepreneurs, while SAB would retain a minority shareholding of 49 percent.
Two years ago local competitor Namibian Breweries Limited (NBL) successfully managed to stave off plans for a SAB brewery at Tsumeb, about 400 km north of the capital Windhoek.
NBL feared at the time it would be forced to close operations at its Swakopmund brewery.
Since then relations between the two competitors have been strained with allegations and counter allegations of unfair practise surfacing repeatedly.
SAB has plants all over southern Africa and is said to hold 98 percent of the regional market. Analysts believe Namibia Breweries is its only competitor worth mentioning.
Government protectionism has so far ensured NBL dominates the Namibian market, but should the latest proposal be accepted, NBL may lose up to 40 percent of its local market share.
NBL's marketing manager Ernst Ender is adamant that the small Namibian market does not justify a third brewery apart from NBL's operations at Swakopmund and Windhoek.
"Due to the size of the market it is totally out of the question to sustain three breweries", he said.
